confidence_notes: I ran three web searches: one for the RBA rate and two for Suzhou prices. The food anchors rest on aggregated cost-of-living pages, mainly That's Mandarin, which gives RMB 30-50 for a local meal and RMB 60-90 for a Western meal, and an undated OkVoyage page. That page gives about 1.9 EUR for a draft beer and about 31 EUR for a mid-range meal for two. I found no Suzhou cappuccino price, so coffee is an estimate based on typical Chinese tier-2 café pricing. I found no current Suzhou cocktail or wine prices. Those two are estimated from the local beer price and typical Chinese urban bar and hotel pricing, with cocktails at about 3.5-4x beer and wine at about 2.5-3x beer. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge, with no live listings checked. They are the least certain, and prices vary with the season and with the area (Jinji Lake, the old town or SIP).
comparable_city_reasoning: Suzhou is a prosperous tier-2 Yangtze Delta city with a large tourist and expat economy. Prices are somewhat below Shanghai and well above inland Chinese cities. Shanghai-adjacent cities such as Wuxi and Hangzhou served as a loose basis.
